note: Métier boundary doctrine. Defines what BRICOLAGE is NOT. Every exclusion must route to a specific métier or disposition.

metier_boundary_doctrine.principle: Bricolage covers low-risk, light household tasks that do not require specialist licensing, safety certification, structural engineering, or access to regulated systems (electrical circuits, plumbing networks, gas, security mechanisms).
metier_boundary_doctrine.core_rule: If a task requires diagnosis of a safety-critical system, modification of a regulated installation, or specialist certification — it is NOT bricolage.
metier_boundary_doctrine.anti-pattern: Bricolage must NEVER become a catch-all category that gives unqualified artisans access to electrical, plumbing, or security work at cheap task prices.
metier_boundary_doctrine.handoff_protocol: STOP → IDENTIFY escape → EXPLAIN to client → DECLARE HORS PÉRIMÈTRE BRICOLAGE → ROUTE to specialist → OBTAIN client approval

tasks_excluded: Any replacement of electrical outlet (prise) or switch (interrupteur)
Any luminaire/light fixture installation requiring wire connection
Electrical socket relocation (for TV mounting or any other reason)
Any work on live wires or circuit conductors

borderline_analysis.description: Swapping a pendant light on an existing intact cable connector — purely mechanical, no wire splicing
borderline_analysis.verdict: CONDITIONAL — depends on whether wire connection is involved. FIXEO should default to ELECTRICITE for any fixture change.
borderline_analysis.reason: Risk of incorrect assessment by non-electrician. Safety and insurance implications.

exclusions.safety_reason: Electrical work on circuits carries electrocution risk, fire risk, and requires compliance with Moroccan NFC 15-100 norms. Incorrect work creates insurance liability. FIXEO frozen electrical doctrine covers this.
exclusions.client_explanation: Pour votre sécurité et la conformité de votre installation, ce travail nécessite un électricien certifié FIXEO.

tasks_excluded: Work on hot water systems (chauffe-eau, thermostats)
Leak repair in walls or under floor

borderline_analysis.description: Tap washer replacement (joint de robinet), shower hose (flexible de douche), siphon cleaning/replacement, toilet cistern float (flotteur) — market classifies these as handyman tasks
borderline_analysis.verdict: CONDITIONAL — FIXEO must decide boundary. Recommended: allow joint de robinet and flexible de douche as bricolage ONLY if water is already off at robinet d'arrêt. Any issue finding the robinet d'arrêt → PLOMBERIE.
borderline_analysis.reason: Consumer-grade maintenance vs plumbing modification. Risk of water damage is contained if stopcock is accessible.

exclusions.safety_reason: Incorrect plumbing work causes water damage, mould, structural damage, and insurance claim disputes in copropriété contexts.
exclusions.client_explanation: Ce travail dépasse le périmètre bricolage. Un plombier FIXEO est nécessaire.

tasks_excluded: Any work on a porte de sécurité / porte blindée mechanism

borderline_analysis.description: Interior door handle (poignée intérieure non-sécurisée) replacement, gâche (strike plate) adjustment on interior door
borderline_analysis.verdict: BRICOLAGE_ALLOWED for non-security interior hardware only. Anything on entrance door or porte palière → SERRURERIE.
borderline_analysis.reason: Security risk from unqualified work on security-grade mechanisms.

exclusions.safety_reason: Security mechanisms require specialist tools and training. FIXEO frozen serrurerie doctrine covers this.

borderline_analysis.description: Adjusting an interior door that sticks (sans fabrication), replacing a standard hinge on an interior door
borderline_analysis.verdict: BRICOLAGE_ALLOWED for adjustment/minor repair. Structural replacement or fabrication → MENUISERIE.
borderline_analysis.reason: Assembly ≠ fabrication. Bricolage can adjust, not build.

borderline_analysis.description: Drilling 8mm holes in standard masonry for anchors (shelf, curtain rod, TV bracket)
borderline_analysis.verdict: BRICOLAGE_ALLOWED for standard anchor-size drilling in non-structural walls. Any uncertainty about wall being load-bearing → STOP → quote.
borderline_analysis.reason: Standard anchor drilling is core bricolage competency. Load-bearing work requires structural engineer.

borderline_analysis.description: Touch-up paint on a small wall scratch
borderline_analysis.verdict: Out of FIXEO standardization scope for now. Very small touch-ups may be possible as add-on, but no standard price.
borderline_analysis.reason: Paint matching is complex. Better in dedicated PEINTURE métier.

borderline_analysis.verdict: CARRELAGE scope — colour matching, adhesive mixing, and finish require specialist.
borderline_analysis.reason: Material matching and technique. Wrong adhesive in wet areas causes structural failure.

tasks_excluded: Work above 2.5m height (above standard step-ladder reach)

borderline_analysis.description: Ceiling-mounted curtain rail (rail plafond) at standard 2.7m ceiling
borderline_analysis.verdict: CONDITIONAL — standard step ladder sufficient for 2.7m with care. Document as client-visible condition. Higher ceilings or inaccessible locations → complexity escape → surcharge or quote.
borderline_analysis.reason: Fall risk above standard step-ladder height. Scaffolding requirement changes economics.

exclusions.safety_reason: Gas work requires certification. No ambiguity — always specialist.

tasks_excluded: Any drilling or anchoring where artisan cannot confirm wall is non-load-bearing
Wall mounting where substrate is unknown/unidentified

borderline_analysis.description: Standard Moroccan apartment masonry — artisan must identify: béton armé, parpaing creux, cloison légère, placo
borderline_analysis.verdict: STOP → identify substrate → confirm non-load-bearing → continue standard price OR escape to conditional/quote if structural concern exists.
borderline_analysis.reason: Reinforced concrete requires specialist tools (SDS-Max, chemical anchors). Hollow block may not support heavy loads. Plasterboard requires stud finder for heavy items.

substrate_complexity_matrix.description: Wall/substrate type affects drilling difficulty, anchor choice, and price eligibility

substrates.standard_fixings: Carbide drill bits, expansion anchors or chemical anchors for heavy loads
substrates.bricolage_eligible: CONDITIONAL — light shelves OK; heavy loads may need quote
substrates.notes: Casablanca 80% of modern buildings per SRC-BRIC-007. Requires percussion drill (marteau-piqueur or SDS).
Standard expansion plugs fail in hollow block — must use Molly anchors.

substrates.standard_fixings: Stud finder required; anchor between studs or into studs
substrates.bricolage_eligible: CONDITIONAL — stud finder required; heavy items need stud anchor
substrates.notes: Heavy TV (>20kg) on placo without stud → REFUSE or structural assessment.

substrates.bricolage_eligible: CONDITIONAL — tile crack risk; surcharge justified
substrates.notes: Risk of tile cracking if bit dulls or angle wrong. Must inform client.

substrates.standard_fixings: Diamond drill bit, very slow speed
substrates.bricolage_eligible: CONDITIONAL — high breakage risk; quote recommended
substrates.notes: High-value substrate. Damage costs significant. Quote preferred.

substrates.bricolage_eligible: CONDITIONAL — standard expansion plugs fail; specialist knowledge needed
substrates.notes: Standard anchors pull out of friable pisé. Riad context is specialty.

client_prescreening_questions.description: Minimum questions before price confirmation per service family

furniture_assembly: Type of furniture? (chair / small / wardrobe / bed / kitchen)
New flat-pack or existing disassembled piece?
Number of items in total visit?
tv_mounting: Bracket supplied by client or needed?
shelf_mounting: Client has brackets or integrated bracket shelf?
curtain_rod: Client has rod and all fixings?
door_adjustment: Does the problem involve the lock or just the frame/hinges?
multi_task_visit: For each: what hardware is client-supplied?
Any electrical or plumbing tasks on the list? (route to specialist)
